explicitLimits: This review does not claim SQLite sole-writer capability acceptance.
A trusted raw DatabaseSync caller can choose and rewrite a local database; target inference is impossible for that internal helper contract and is outside the supported package boundary.

Dynamic aliases, assigned callback effects, dependency internals and every arbitrary code execution path are not closed by finite static inventories.
Portable export/bundle/signing/configuration and installation metadata remain explicit file-owned compatibility/output surfaces; they are not operational state authority.

localOnlyLimitations: Local validation only; current hosted validation remains required.

publicAuthorityBinding.evidence: Validates command/input, resolves the project target, and invokes the canonical executor with trusted authority/runtime context out of actor-controlled input.
Maps all six commands to canonical services; maintenance/restore exceptions use dedicated admission, ordinary commands use withProjectStorage, and backup is read-only on source.
The supported ./integration package surface re-exports executeForgeLoopCommand, resource reads and command definitions.
MCP derives tools from canonical command metadata, strips actor authority/runtime fields, applies policy, then delegates to executeForgeLoopCommand.
Integration resources use read-only withProjectStorage/read snapshots.
getOperationalStore(target), safe destination, and admitted db/target are the only public backup inputs.
AsyncLocalStorage store must match target path or realpath; mismatches fail with E_TASK_CONTEXT_MISMATCH.
Checks maintenance/legacy locks and marker, bootstraps only fresh writable projects, refuses mixed legacy state, and passes projectAdmission to SQLite.
Opened database must match canonical path, regular-file/dev/ino/root identity and non-symlink sidecars before configuration/reuse.
NPM exports are only the package root CLI and ./integration; internal storage/index.js is not a package subpath.

internalHelperContract.conclusion: No independent public misbinding regression is warranted for the low-level exporter/backup helpers under the supported threat model.

exportTask.contract: Trusted caller supplies authoritative db, taskId and portable destination; helper exports a consistent read snapshot and does not infer a source target.

exportDatabase.contract: Trusted caller supplies authoritative db, destination and optional attachmentRoot; every referenced attachment is verified against size and SHA-256 before copy.

backupProjectStorage.contract: Trusted caller supplies committed db, source target and destination; the service records database/inventory digests, verifies references and rejects changed bytes.

internalHelperContract.supportedPublicBinding: storage-backup binds target through command-runtime -> COMMAND_EXECUTORS -> withProjectStorage -> operationalContext -> getOperationalStore and passes that store.db/target to backupProjectStorage.
internalHelperContract.packageBoundary: The source barrel exports helpers for repository-local consumers, but package.json exports only the CLI and ./integration. Raw DatabaseSync callers can already rewrite any local database they are authorized to open; that is an internal trusted-caller contract, not a reachable actor-controlled public target swap.
internalHelperContract.docsBinding: docs/SQLITE_MIGRATION_MATRIX.md:939-941 records that internal exportTask/exportDatabase are not package export surfaces and that per-call maintenance ownership/aliases/dependencies/transitive proof remain open.

soleWriterAudit.requirement: docs/SQLITE_MIGRATION_PLAN.md:281-290 requires sole SQLite operational authority, migrated or explicitly exported file consumers, tested migration/recovery/backup/restore/downgrade, old-client exclusion, obsolete writer removal and CLI/MCP/API/package/platform checks.
soleWriterAudit.currentSupportedSurfaceConclusion: Within the reviewed built-in CLI/integration/MCP boundary, no concrete public misbinding or legacy operational writer was found. Ordinary dispatch and direct writer helpers route through canonical SQLite admission; legacy operational state is refused, and explicit portable outputs remain outside canonical authority.
